description: Conversiono Psychology Framework — maps behavioral features to psychological states and interventions

states.label: Loss Aversion
states.description: User perceives potential loss as more painful than equivalent gain. Manifests as prolonged price inspection and hesitation at checkout — the user wants the product but fears making a bad financial decision.

interventions.message: This price expires in {countdown} — save {amount} today

states.label: Decision Fatigue
states.description: Extended browsing with repeated direction changes indicates cognitive overload. The user has been evaluating too many options and their decision-making quality is degrading.
states.academic_basis: Baumeister et al., Ego Depletion (1998); Iyengar & Lepper, Choice Overload (2000)

interventions.message: Most popular choice: {product_name} — chosen by {pct}% of shoppers
Not sure which to pick? Compare your top 3 side by side

states.label: Decision Uncertainty
states.description: User shows interest but cannot commit — hovering over action buttons without clicking, scrolling back to re-read details. They need more information or social validation to feel confident.
states.academic_basis: Festinger, Cognitive Dissonance (1957); Cialdini, Social Proof (1984)

interventions.message: {count} people bought this in the last 24 hours

states.label: UI Frustration
states.description: Rapid repeated clicks on the same area and erratic mouse movement indicate the user is fighting the interface. Something is broken, unresponsive, or confusing.
states.academic_basis: Nielsen, Usability Heuristics (1994); Ceaparu et al., Frustration with Technology (2004)

interventions.message: Having trouble? Chat with us — we're here to help
Something not working? Let us know and get 10% off

states.label: Abandonment Intent
states.description: User is actively trying to leave — mouse moving toward browser controls, switching tabs, or triggering back navigation. This is the last chance to retain them.
states.academic_basis: Weinberg, Exit Intent Detection (2013); Park & Fader, Customer Retention Models (2004)

interventions.message: Wait — here's {discount}% off your order. Use code {code}
We'll save your cart — enter your email to pick up where you left off

states.label: Trust Gap
states.description: User is interested in purchasing but does not feel safe completing the transaction. They spend excessive time on price and payment details, looking for reasons to trust or distrust the store.
states.academic_basis: McKnight et al., Trust in E-Commerce (2002); Kim et al., Online Consumer Trust (2008)

interventions.message: Secure checkout — SSL encrypted, PCI compliant

states.label: Price Shock
states.description: User is fixated on pricing but not progressing toward checkout. The price is higher than their mental anchor — they expected it to cost less and are now reconsidering.
states.academic_basis: Thaler, Mental Accounting (1985); Ariely, Predictably Irrational — Anchoring Effect (2008)

interventions.message: That's only {daily_cost}/day — less than a coffee

states.label: Approach-Avoidance Conflict
states.description: User oscillates between buying signals (adding to cart, clicking CTA) and retreat signals (hesitating, scrolling back). They want the product but an unresolved concern is holding them back.
states.academic_basis: Lewin, Approach-Avoidance Conflict (1935); Miller, Goal Gradient Hypothesis (1944)

interventions.message: Try it risk-free — free returns within {days} days
